ConnectCall Solutions is a BPO company handling customer support for multiple clients. The
company has 800 employees working in night shifts. The HR director, Mr. Mehta, conducted an
internal survey to understand why employee turnover was high. He compiled the following real
statements from employees:
Employee A (Ravi, age 22, works for 8 months):
"I earn just enough to pay for my shared room and food. But last month, the company delayed
salaries by two weeks. I had to borrow money. Also, there's no transport facility at night. I fear
walking to the bus stop after the shift. I'm thinking of quitting."
Employee B (Neha, age 25, works for 2 years):
"I have a decent salary and the company provides cab service at night. But honestly, I feel invisible
here. My team leader never says 'good job.' I have won 'Employee of the Month' twice, but no one
celebrated it. My colleagues don't include me in their WhatsApp group. I eat lunch alone every
day."
Employee C (Arjun, age 30, works for 5 years):
"I have a good salary, my own house, and a supportive team. But for the last two years, I have been
doing the same troubleshooting calls. I have asked for cross-training in chat support and voice
process, but my request is always ignored. I feel my career has stopped growing."
Employee D (Priya, age 40, works for 10 years):
"I am a senior team lead. I have a high salary, a car, respect from my team, and challenging
projects. Last year, I completed an MBA while working. Now I want to design a new training module
for freshers. I have ideas to improve the entire onboarding process. But my manager says, 'Just
follow the existing manual.' I feel I have more to offer."
Employee E (Sunil, age 28, works for 3 years):
"I have no complaints about salary or safety. My team is friendly and my work is interesting. But last
month, I was passed over for a promotion despite having better numbers than the person who got
promoted. My manager said, 'Seniority matters more than performance.' I feel humiliated and
underappreciated."
Based on the case of ConnectCall Solutions:
i). Identify the highest level of Maslow's Hierarchy of Needs that is currently unfulfilled for each of
the five employees (A, B, C, D, E).
ii) For employees A and D, explain what specific action the company should take to fulfill their unmet
need. Justify your answer using Maslow's theory.
(2½+1½ = 4 marks)
guide: Maslow: physiological → safety → social → esteem → self-actualization.
Physiological: basic living needs. Safety: security. Social: belonging.
Esteem: respect and recognition. Self-actualization: realizing potential.
In a case, identify the unmet need using the employee’s specific statement. Multiple unmet needs may appear.
tip: A: safety is the highest explicit unmet level, with physiological concerns also present. B: esteem is higher than the also-unmet belonging need. C: blocked development supports self-actualization; an esteem interpretation needs explicit justification. D: self-actualization. E: esteem. For A provide timely pay and safe transport; for D allow meaningful creative contribution to training. These are reasoned interpretations, not an official key.
